title: When no free frame remains
purpose: Explain a reference to absent B while all user RAM frames are occupied.
requiredChecks: Process1 table is A/page0/frame6/resident, B/page1/absent, C/page2/frame3/resident, D/page3/frame2/resident.
Available user frames are all occupied: frame2 D,3 C,4 F,5 H,6 A,7 E.
Backing storage contains B and G, with B the referenced missing page.
The request to load B requires selecting a victim; diagram does not invent a selected victim or place B into a free frame.
alt: Page B causes a fault while all user frames are occupied, so a victim frame must be selected
prompt: Create a NEW original English technical blog diagram. White background, crisp dark navy large sans-serif labels, flat blue/teal outlined shapes, generous whitespace, simple unambiguous connectors, no decorative art, no logos or watermark. TITLE "When no free frame remains". NEW wide readable layout with THREE panels. Left "Process 1 page table" with headers "Page","Contents","Frame","Present" and four exact rows "0 | A | 6 | 1", "1 | B | — | 0", "2 | C | 3 | 1", "3 | D | 2 | 1". Highlight B row and add nearby text "Reference to B → page fault". Middle "Physical memory — occupied user frames" with six equal entries "Frame 2: D", "Frame 3: C", "Frame 4: F", "Frame 5: H", "Frame 6: A", "Frame 7: E". Do not show any free entry; a note below reads "Other frames reserved". Right "Backing storage" with two boxes B and G. A dashed arrow from backing storage B toward the middle panel is labeled "Select a victim before loading B", and it terminates at the panel border, not a chosen frame. Footer exactly "No free user frame: page replacement is required". Keep all numbers consistent, no invented victim or duplicate B in RAM, no cylindrical disk artwork.
